aliases: mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA type-c
summary: MOTS-c is a peptide in the mitochondrial peptides class (mitochondria-derived; AMPK and folate-cycle effects reported). Europe PMC indexes 277 publications naming it or a listed alias in a title or abstract, including 4 randomized controlled trials and 1 clinical trials of any design, as of 2026-09-14. The strongest evidence tier in that literature is human clinical trials. This page reports what those studies state, sentence by sentence, with each statement tied to its source and labeled by the kind of evidence it is. It does not recommend use, and it does not translate study doses into anything personal.

faq.question: Has MOTS-c been tested in humans?
faq.answer: Yes. Europe PMC indexes 1 clinical trials and 4 randomized controlled trials naming MOTS-c or a listed alias in the title or abstract. The evidence table above lists the ones in this record's ledger with their design and sample size; check the study name, since an alias can refer to a different formulation of the same molecule.

faq.question: What kind of evidence exists for MOTS-c?
faq.answer: The strongest tier is human clinical trial: human clinical trials. Every claim on this page carries its own tier, because a compound with one human trial and forty animal studies is described by both facts, not the better one.

faq.question: Is MOTS-c an approved medicine?
faq.answer: No ChEMBL record matches MOTS-c or its aliases, which usually means it has not entered a registered clinical development programme. It is not an approved medicine in any jurisdiction this record has checked.

faq.question: Which species has MOTS-c been studied in?
faq.answer: Studies in this record's ledger report work in: Humans, Mice, Rats. Findings in one species do not transfer to another, and weight-normalized doses in particular do not scale linearly between them.
